parole.significato: Genitival interfix used to link elements in some compounds
parole.testo: * In most words from an old plural genitive, Old Swedish -a, from Old Norse -a, e.g. gästabud (“feast, banquet”), from Old Swedish gæsta buþ, genitive plural of gæster (“guest”), modern Swedish gäst. * In some words from an old singular genitive, Old Swedish -a, -ar, from Old Norse -ar, e.g. dialect
From Old Swedish īlla, from Old Norse ílla, illa, adverb formation of Swedish ill, Old Swedish īlder, Old Norse íllr, illr. Related to English ill.

parole.significato: anger (a strong feeling of displeasure, hostility or antagonism towards someone or something)
parole.testo: From Old Swedish ilzka (noun), from Old Norse íllska, derivative of Old Swedish ilzker (“evil”, adjective), Old Norse *íllskr, to the same stem as ill (adjective), illa (adverb); Old Swedish ilder (adjective), Old Swedish illa (adverb); Old Norse íllr (adjective), ílla (adverb), from Proto-Germanic

parole.significato: to spoil, to ruin, to dishonour
parole.testo: From Old Norse skemmd (“shame, disgrace”), from Old Swedish skæmma ("to dishonour") and the reflexive skæmmas ("to be ashamed"), same as Icelandic skemma, Danish skæmme, Middle Low German schemen, German schämen; related to Swedish skam (“shame”).

Inherited from Late Old Swedish sø̄der, sø̄dher, sudher, from Old Norse suðr, with the ø-umlaut from södre, Old Swedish syþre, Old Norse syðri (comparative); compare the ø in Norwegian sør, Danish sønder. Doublet of syd. Compare dialectal Danish sønder, Old Norse sunnr, Old High German sundar. Other

parole.significato: the quality or state of being appealing or pleasant or sympathetic, grace or loveliness or coquetry
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Swedish ynnist. From the verb unna, from Old Norse unna (“to bestow, grant”), but also related to ynne of the same sense, to Old Swedish ynni, to Old Norse yndi. First attested in 1501.
